title: One request, from tag to merged PR
note: Beeline is read-only in this teardown: the source was cloned and read, never run, so the trace is a code-level walk of one request, not a runtime capture.
example_input: @codex the corner status line wraps onto two lines on small phones. fix it and open a PR.

steps.title: A tag becomes a command
steps.narrative: A person tags the agent in a repository Room: fix the wrapping status line and open a PR. The message itself authorizes nothing - routeHumanMessage turns it into a durable agent_commands row, with the human message recorded as the chain's root. Orders will travel down this chain; reports will come back one step up.
steps.representation:
Room message: "@codex the corner status line wraps onto
two lines on small phones. fix it and open a PR."
  -> routeHumanMessage -> agent_commands row
     (root_source_message_id = the human message)

modules.label: routeHumanMessage: a human message becomes commands

steps.title: The order reaches the helper
steps.narrative: The paired machine's helper learns of the order over the machine's one live socket - helpers never poll. The body assembles the turn: the Room transcript as context, Beeline's MCP surface, and the standing instructions for the place the turn will run in.
steps.representation:
live socket -> DaemonApiClient -> command claimed
prompt assembly: transcript + beeline MCP tools
  + CORNER_AUTHOR_CONTRACT for corner turns

modules.label: DaemonApiClient: the agent's registration on the machine socket

steps.title: A session opens under bwrap
steps.narrative: The helper spawns the operator's own harness under bubblewrap and speaks ACP to it: session/new, then session/prompt. In a top-level Room the mount plan keeps the checkout read-only; the harness's own loop - not Beeline - runs the turn, with its own sign-in and its native session.
steps.representation:
bwrap(mount plan: Room = checkout read-only)
  -> harness process
ACP session/new -> sessionId
ACP session/prompt -> the request text

modules.label: session/new: every ACP session the daemon opens

steps.title: open_corner: the brief is authorized
steps.narrative: Asked to do repository work, the agent calls open_corner. The server resolves the brief - a Markdown spec plus file manifest - against the dispatching human message, which is the authorization; the short objective is navigation only. The corner opens in state opened and moves at once to implement.
steps.representation:
open_corner(objective <= 24 words, brief spec <= 16,000 chars)
  -> resolveCornerBriefApproval(dispatching message)
  -> corner_facts row; lifecycle: opened -> implement

modules.label: resolveCornerBriefApproval: the dispatching message authorizes the brief

steps.title: A worktree is cut and synced
steps.narrative: On the helper, the corner gets a worktree at beeline/corners/<cornerId>, cut from a shared bare clone on the corner's feature branch, with a repository-scoped GitHub App token installed as a worktree-only credential helper. Before the turn - and every later turn - the worktree syncs to origin/<branch>: fast-forward, rebase, or realign on conflict.
steps.representation:
<root>/beeline/corners/<cornerId>  (git worktree)
credential.helper = x-access-token / $GH_TOKEN (this repo only)
sync: fetch -> ff | rebase | realign (never force-push)

steps.title: Push, PR, and live checks
steps.narrative: The agent works in the worktree, pushes the branch and opens the pull request. The Room shows the corner card with the PR and its checks. The server never trusts a stored verdict: check state is read live from the PR head's rollup, and webhooks only trigger re-reads.
steps.representation:
git push origin <feature_branch>; gh pr create
webhook -> prChecksStatus(cornerId)
  -> GraphQL statusCheckRollup on the live head

modules.label: prChecksStatus: the live check read behind the gate
advanceCorner: checks state, green wakes the reviewer

steps.title: Review: a yes on the exact head
steps.narrative: Green checks dispatch the Room's configured reviewer - never the implementer. Its approve_merge PASS writes the one approval row for this corner, bound to the PR number and head SHA. A Workspace owner or admin can give the same yes from the phone. A hold from any person would veto all of it, and a new commit cancels the yes.
steps.representation:
corner_merge_approvals: (corner_id, approved_by,
  pull_request_number, head_sha) - one row per corner
gate = checks green AND yes on this head AND no hold

modules.label: cornerMergeGate: who may supply the yes

steps.title: landCorner: merge and archive
steps.narrative: The PASS wakes the implementer, whose merge_corner runs the one merge path: the brief must still assign repository work, the gate is read live once more, the head is claimed so no second attempt can race it, and GitHub squash-merges - or enqueues, when a merge queue is configured. Confirmation archives the corner, cancels its pending commands and enqueues the branch for deletion; the helper reaps the worktree.
steps.representation:
landCorner: assertCornerBriefAllowsMerge
  -> gate live -> claimCornerMergeAttempt(head)
  -> squash merge -> archived; branch deletion enqueued

modules.label: landCorner / landCornerOutcome: the one merge path
recordPersonMergeYes: a person's yes lands at once
